topic_summary: Analysis of free movement within the European Union as a contested kernel where the federation-membership commitment is read differently by integration-primary and member-sovereignty-primary interpretations. Each reading produces structurally different constraints with distinct cost-bearer sets: displaced local labor under integration primacy versus constrained mobility under sovereignty primacy.

key_entities: European Union (supranational federation with treaty-based authority)
Member States (sovereign nations with treaty obligations)
Mobile EU Citizens (workers exercising free movement rights)
Local Labor Markets (destination-state workers facing competition)
European Court of Justice (interpretive authority for treaty law)
key_tensions: Supranational treaty authority vs national sovereignty (ECJ vs member state parliaments)
Mobile worker rights vs local labor market protection (EU citizens vs destination-state workers)
Economic integration efficiency vs democratic accountability (market optimization vs electoral mandate)
key_mechanisms: Treaty of Rome Article 45 enforcement (ECJ rulings override national restrictions)
Welfare magnet dynamics (benefit access differentials drive migration patterns)
key_absences: Fiscal federalism mechanisms (no EU-level unemployment insurance or wage equalization)
Exit cost asymmetries (high-skill vs low-skill mobility barriers)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The federation-membership treaty commitment establishing free movement as a fundamental right within the EU legal order
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: ECJ holds interpretive supremacy over treaty meaning; member states retain implementation authority but cannot override treaty obligations

readings.commitment: Free movement is constitutive of the single market; restrictions are presumptively illegitimate unless narrowly justified
readings.authority_grounding: ECJ jurisprudence prioritizing market integration and individual rights over member state discretion
readings.expected_structural_delta: Mobile workers enter beneficiary set; local labor markets and welfare systems enter victim set; high suppression of national restrictions

readings.commitment: Free movement is conditional on member state consent; states retain authority to protect national labor markets and welfare systems
readings.authority_grounding: National constitutional orders and democratic accountability; treaty as compact among sovereigns
readings.expected_structural_delta: Local labor markets enter beneficiary set; mobile workers enter victim set via restricted access; high preservation of national regulatory autonomy

readings.commitment: Free movement operates within bounds of proportionality; legitimate national interests constrain but do not eliminate mobility rights
readings.authority_grounding: Treaty subsidiarity principle; ECJ proportionality doctrine balancing integration and sovereignty
readings.expected_structural_delta: Graduated constraint structure; beneficiary/victim sets vary by policy domain; moderate suppression of both unrestricted mobility and blanket restrictions

axes.structural_delta: Free movement as constitutive right; national restrictions presumptively illegitimate
axes.primary_observable: ECJ case law strike-down rate of national mobility restrictions; treaty infringement proceedings
axes.selection_reason: First reading of contested kernel; highest epsilon; captures ECJ-driven integration logic

axes.structural_delta: Free movement as conditional treaty obligation; states retain labor market protection authority
axes.primary_observable: National restriction implementation rate; political resistance to ECJ rulings; Brexit-style exit threats
axes.selection_reason: Second reading of contested kernel; inverts beneficiary/victim structure; captures member state resistance

axes.structural_delta: Free movement bounded by proportionality; graduated constraint structure across policy domains
axes.primary_observable: ECJ proportionality test outcomes; variance in restriction legitimacy by policy area
axes.selection_reason: Third reading of contested kernel; captures institutional compromise position; moderate epsilon

axes.structural_delta: Absence of EU-level unemployment insurance or wage equalization mechanisms amplifies local cost concentration
axes.primary_observable: EU budget share of GDP vs US federal budget; absence of cross-border automatic stabilizers
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: structural precondition but lower analytical priority than kernel readings; captured in omega

axes.structural_delta: High-skill workers face low exit costs; low-skill workers face high barriers despite formal rights
axes.primary_observable: Migration rate variance by skill level; credential recognition barriers; language requirements
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: implementation friction rather than kernel-level structural difference

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Absence of EU-level redistribution mechanisms amplifies local cost concentration
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Structural precondition captured across all three readings; mountain status makes it analytically simpler than kernel readings

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Skill-stratified mobility barriers despite formal rights equality
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Implementation friction rather than kernel-level constitutional contest; lower centrality

omegas.description: Would EU-level unemployment insurance or wage equalization collapse the kernel contest by removing local cost concentration? Or would it shift the contest to fiscal sovereignty vs redistribution authority?
omegas.source: Deferred axis fiscal_federalism_absence + Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan)

omegas.description: Does repeated ECJ override of national restrictions trigger legitimacy crisis (sovereignty_primary reading gains authority) or normalize integration (integration_primary reading consolidates)? Path-dependent outcome.

Brexit exit demonstrates sovereignty_primary reading can override integration_primary via constitutional rupture. Does this validate sovereignty_primary as the true kernel reading, or prove integration_primary requires coercive enforcement?
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) + sovereignty_primary observable

omegas.description: Empirical evidence on welfare magnet effects is contested. If magnets are weak, integration_primary cost-bearer set shrinks. If strong, sovereignty_primary legitimacy increases. Measurement uncertainty affects kernel reading validity.

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel decomposition successfully identified three structurally distinct readings with inverted beneficiary/victim structures. Fiscal federalism absence and exit cost asymmetry appropriately deferred as lower-priority structural conditions rather than kernel-level contests.
